clue.text: Exact replica of small fruit stone

clue.text: Wings of swan covering dull part of flower

clue.text: King of Mercia once listened to proposal

explanation.walkthrough: Offa sounds like 'offer' in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was an eighth-century Anglo-Saxon ruler of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke.

clue.text: Artist and daughter wearing relative's fashion label

D is short for daughter in genealogies

explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is a crossword staple for an artist; 'wearing' means the relative goes round the others.

clue.text: New title about way of working provided recurring theme

clue.text: Light-fingered types with permission to interrupt meals

clue.text: Dance by graduate following sport

clue.text: Steel drum keeping time with first of trumpeters in procession

clue.text: Captives welcoming year in this part of Wales

clue.text: Tremor caused by dessert wine

clue.text: Police search for suspect in flowering garden close to Parliament

clue.text: Card for sailor to turn over?

explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of a pack of cards used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Plant obscured by yellow heather

clue.text: Setter leaving bread to go off

clue.text: East European given piece of butter to turn into culinary paste

clue.text: Bear is swimming around island in a chilly part of the world

clue.text: Crikey — jack held by boy playing against Spain

explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges BOY into BYO, and 'held by' puts J inside.

clue.text: Judge trading shilling for time in estate

clue.text: Staff allowed to get something to eat

clue.text: King at end of extra pilgrimage returned with eastern prince

clue.text: Substantial addition to pure alcohol

clue.text: Old nurse close to commode encountering aroma that's characteristic of old age

clue.text: Bit of wood glue
